title: EGA VI. Plans, notations, problèmes ouverts : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a short loose sheet of editorial and planning notes for the projected EGA VI (descent). It belongs with the planning material and is not continuous with the previous page, which is SGA4-style text on fibre functors of topoi, paragraph 7.9.

(1) 'Recommandation importante: Partout où c'est possible, employer "fid. plat quasi-compact" pour "couvrant".' This is a terminological and methodological decision. Wherever possible, the descent chapter should state results for faithfully flat quasi-compact (fpqc) morphisms rather than for abstract 'covering' morphisms of a topology. Concretely, the descent statements would be made for the explicit class of fpqc morphisms, as in SGA1 VIII and EGA IV 2.

(2) '(pré)-Relations d'équivalence en plusieurs [dimensions?] ?? (R_0^i) ⇇ (R_1^{ij})' (circled). The diagram is a family of objects R_0^i, together with objects R_1^{ij} each carrying two maps, to R_0^i and R_0^j. In modern terms this is a 'multi-object' (pre-)equivalence relation or groupoid. Equivalently it is a groupoid whose object of objects is the coproduct ⨿R_0^i and whose arrows are ⨿R_1^{ij}. It is the shape of descent data relative to a covering family {U_i → X}, with R_1^{ij} = U_i ×_X U_j. It is also the shape of a quotient problem for a family of schemes glued along relations, which generalises the gluing of schemes in EGA I. The '??' records an unresolved question: whether and how to set up the quotient and effectivity theory for such indexed (pre-)equivalence relations. Grothendieck may have wanted it in parallel with the single-object theory (SGA3 Exp. V, Gabriel). An alternative reading of the half-legible word, 'dimensions', would point to higher simplicial truncations (R_0, R_1, R_2, ...), but the indices i, ij favour the family reading.

Both items serve the organisation of EGA VI (descent, quotients, representability).

deep.surprise_reason: These are planning notes: a terminology choice (fpqc for 'covering') and a query about indexed equivalence relations. Both are standard material in FGA, SGA1 and SGA3. The only mild interest is documentary: they show Grothendieck intended EGA VI to be phrased in fpqc terms.
transcription_corrections: 'fid[?] plat qu[?] comp[?]' should read 'fid. plat quasi-compact' (abbreviated 'fid. plat qu. comp.').
A crossed-out symbol precedes '(R_0^i)', and the whole formula (R_0^i) ⇇ (R_1^{ij}) is encircled.

The second line under '(pré)-Relations d'équivalence en plusieurs' is barely legible. 'dimensions' is uncertain; the upper index on R_1 is 'ij'. The '??' stands between this word and the circled formula.
